lines.trans: Vika, please come to the window!
Well, do you not want to see me at all?
Alright, then at least just say goodbye to me.
Aha, are you playing hide-and-seek with me?
You are acting just like in kindergarten!
And look who is talking right now!
And I could have fallen from here at any moment.
Look, if I fall, it will be on your conscience!
Max, you fool, what are you doing out there!
Do not worry, everything is secure here.
Be careful, Max, hold on tight!
Good Lord, Max, did you fall!

examples.trans: As one wise man said, the sun shines equally on everyone.

examples.text: Теперь весь ресторан полностью на мне.
examples.trans: Now the entire restaurant is completely on my shoulders.

examples.text: По поводу ресторана я тебе уже говорил, Дима.
examples.trans: I already told you about the restaurant, Dima.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Надеюсь, я умру не от твоего блюда!
examples.trans: I hope I do not die from your dish!

examples.text: Значит, она просто удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: That means she simply deleted your number.

examples.text: Она удалила твой номер.
examples.trans: She deleted your number.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овесть'). Common feminine noun meaning 'conscience' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Смотри, если упаду, это будет на твоей совести!
examples.trans: Look, if I fall, it will be on your conscience!

examples.text: Ты просто бессовестный обманщик!
examples.trans: You are simply a shameless liar!

examples.text: Имей совесть!
examples.trans: Have a heart!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'fool' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Состряпать еду каждый дурак может, даже я.
examples.trans: Any fool can whip up food, even I can.

examples.text: Состряпать может любой дурак, а ты попробуй приготовить!
examples.trans: Any fool can whip something up, but try to actually cook!

examples.text: Макс, дурак, что ты там делаешь!
examples.trans: Max, you fool, what are you doing out there!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что ты там делал, просто яйца варил?
examples.trans: What did you do there, just boil eggs?

examples.text: Это наша свадьба, где хотим, там и празднуем!
examples.trans: It is our wedding, we celebrate wherever we want!

examples.text: Что там у тебя случилось с машиной?
examples.trans: What happened with your truck down there?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are doing', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: Что ты там делал, просто яйца варил?
examples.trans: What did you do there, just boil eggs?

examples.text: Дима, а ты что здесь на кухне делаешь?
examples.trans: Dima, and what are you doing here in the kitchen?

examples.text: Макс, дурак, что ты там делаешь!
examples.trans: Max, you fool, what are you doing out there!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Продай его нам, одной проблемой меньше станет.
examples.trans: Sell it to us, and you will have one less problem.

examples.text: Да ничего не рухнет, главное в ресторане что?
examples.trans: Nothing will collapse, what is the main thing in a restaurant?

examples.text: Что главное в ресторане, конечно кухня и еда!
examples.trans: What is the main thing in a restaurant, the kitchen and food, of course!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'worry'.

examples.text: Не волнуйся.
examples.trans: Don't worry.

examples.text: Я волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I'm nervous.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, не буду.
examples.trans: Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если я уйду, здесь всё рухнет без меня!
examples.trans: If I leave, everything here will collapse without me!

examples.text: Дима, а ты что здесь на кухне делаешь?
examples.trans: Dima, and what are you doing here in the kitchen?

examples.text: Да не волнуйся ты, здесь всё надёжно.
examples.trans: Do not worry, everything is secure here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если я уйду, здесь всё рухнет без меня!
examples.trans: If I leave, everything here will collapse without me!

examples.text: Это всё, Костя, между нами всё кончено.
examples.trans: That is it, Kostya, everything is over between us.

examples.text: Слушай, Ева, наверное, всё-таки нет.
examples.trans: Listen, Eva, probably not after all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'дёжно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да не волнуйся ты, здесь всё надёжно.
examples.trans: Do not worry, everything is secure here.

examples.text: Дверь закрыта надёжно.
examples.trans: The door is securely locked.

examples.text: Мы готовы надёжно защищать вас везде.
examples.trans: We are ready to reliably protect you everywhere.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Осторожно, Макс, держись крепче!
examples.trans: Be careful, Max, hold on tight!

examples.text: Мужчина, поосторожнее можно, отойдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Sir, could you be more careful, step back, please!

examples.text: Тише, Ваня, осторожно!
examples.trans: Easy, Vanya, be careful!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hang in there'.

related.gloss: not to hang in there (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?

examples.text: Надо держаться от неё подальше.
examples.trans: I need to stay further away from her.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Осторожно, Макс, держись крепче!
examples.trans: Be careful, Max, hold on tight!

examples.text: Держи его крепче, Ваня!
examples.trans: Hold him tighter, Vanya!

examples.text: Дети крепко спят.
examples.trans: The children are sleeping soundly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'Lord', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Господи, Макс, ты что, упал!
examples.trans: Good Lord, Max, did you fall!

examples.text: Господи, что случилось?
examples.trans: Good Lord, what happened?

examples.text: Ах, господи!
examples.trans: Oh, Lord!
